title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

topics.title: Electron emission and the work function

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the measurements of e/m by Thomson and of e by Millikan established the electron as a universal particle of known mass.
Define the work function of a metal and use the electron volt as a unit of energy.
Distinguish thermionic, field and photoelectric emission by the way energy is supplied to free electrons.
Describe the observations of Hertz, Hallwachs and Lenard that revealed photoelectric emission.
Explain why different metals need light above different threshold frequencies to emit electrons.

topics.title: Experimental study of the photoelectric effect

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the photocurrent and the saturation current to the intensity of the incident light.
Define the stopping potential and relate it to the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons.
Interpret photocurrent versus collector potential curves for light of different frequencies.

topics.title: Photoelectric effect and the wave theory of light

concepts.learning_objective: State what the classical wave picture of light predicts for photoelectric emission.
Explain which observations of the photoelectric effect the wave picture fails to explain and why.
Apply Einstein's equation Kmax = h nu - phi0 to calculate kinetic energies and stopping potentials.
Calculate the threshold frequency of a metal from its work function using nu0 = phi0/h.
Interpret the straight-line graph of stopping potential against frequency to obtain h/e and the threshold frequency.

topics.title: Particle nature of light: the photon

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the energy and momentum of a photon and the photon flux of a monochromatic source.
State the properties of photons, including their neutrality and behaviour in collisions.
Apply the de Broglie relation lambda = h/p to material particles and photons.
Explain why matter waves are significant for sub-atomic particles but not for everyday objects.
